name: og-32-first-self-maintaining-protocell
title: First Self-Maintaining Protocell
gate_reason: Gate C (self-compartmentation), the structurally-informed successor to og-31's partial, reduced-coupling result. og-31 showed that an endogenous membrane pays for itself on persistence under a reduced-coupling model (retention/access as separate knobs), explicitly NOT a molecular-dynamics permeability. Study 32 tightens that coupling: the amphiphile composition is run through short molecular dynamics (viva-openmm Martini 3 CG-MD) to inform the membrane permeability, which sets metabolite retention, which feeds back on the metabolism - so composition informs permeability informs retention, a tighter chain than og-31's proxy. The gate is met only if, at input fluxes held equal to a no-endogenous-membrane ablation, the compartment (i) maintains its own membrane (net amphiphile production >= degradation) AND (ii) beats that ablation on productive flux or persistence. Self-maintenance is taken in its measurable form (integrity + benefit over the matched null), NOT strict autopoietic closure. Guardrail: the metabolism is the sustained A1 carbon-fixing network, not autocatalytic (A2 is refuted under vent conditions) - the claim under test is that a persisting network can build and maintain a membrane that earns its cost, never that the chemistry self-amplifies. Permeability method: Option B (MD-informed structural proxy - short CG-MD -> bilayer thickness -> effective permeability via a published solubility-diffusion relation); the PMF-resolved closure (Option A, the real viva-md-membrane wrapper) is a tracked, compute-budgeted follow-up recorded in discovery_implications, not a buried caveat. Wording stays precisely MD-informed, not PMF-resolved. RESULT: self-maintaining in the measurable form (verdict qualified) - integrity maintained and a persistence benefit over the matched ablation, with throughput feed-limited (not improved) as in og-31.
claim: A composite coupling the endogenous vent-fed metabolism to an endogenous membrane - with the membrane's permeability informed by short molecular dynamics of its amphiphile composition, a tighter coupling than og-31's retention/access proxy - self-maintains in the measurable sense: at input fluxes held equal to a no-endogenous-membrane ablation, the membrane is rebuilt by metabolism-supplied amphiphiles at least as fast as it degrades (net production >= degradation) AND the enclosed system exceeds the ablation on persistence (standing metabolite pool ~2.0x). Throughput is not improved (0.79x, feed-limited) - so the benefit is retention, not faster chemistry, and the verdict is qualified, not an unconditional pass. The metabolism is the sustained A1 carbon-fixing network (not autocatalytic; A2 refuted), so the result is that a persisting network can make and keep a membrane that pays its way on persistence, within a located window (integrity holds up to a degradation rate k_deg <= ~0.01/s, and the persistence benefit tracks the MD composition).
question: Can a vent-fed metabolism and an endogenous membrane be coupled so the membrane encloses and is maintained by the metabolism - and does the enclosed system persist and function better than the same metabolism with no membrane, at equal feeds?
hypothesis: Coupling the study-29/30 reaction network to the study-31 amphiphile/membrane closure yields a compartment that retains metabolites against leakage, is replenished by metabolism-supplied amphiphiles faster than it degrades, and sustains higher productive flux or persistence than a membrane-less control at equal feeds - with the membrane's permeability informed by short molecular dynamics of its composition, so retention follows more directly from the chemistry than an imposed parameter does. If net amphiphile production falls below degradation, or the compartment fails to beat the matched null, no self-maintenance is claimed.
objective: Join the study-30 reactive transport and study-29 kinetics to the study-31 amphiphile pool in one Vivarium composite, with membrane permeability informed by short molecular dynamics of the amphiphile composition and gating the metabolite exchange; track membrane integrity (production vs degradation), standing metabolite pool and productive flux; and test both self-maintenance criteria against a matched no-endogenous-membrane ablation with input fluxes held equal - reporting a net cost honestly if that is the result.
proposed_mechanisms: metabolism-supplied amphiphile production vs membrane degradation (net integrity)
composition-informed permeability from short molecular dynamics (tightening og-31's retention/access proxy)
permeability-gated metabolite retention feeding back on the enclosed metabolism
benefit (persistence and/or productive flux) over a matched membrane-less control at equal feeds
proposed_models_methods: Short Martini 3 CG-MD of two amphiphile chain-length compositions -> bilayer thickness -> effective permeability via a published solubility-diffusion structure->permeability relation [viva-openmm / martini_openmm, run on the mini; Option B = MD-informed structural proxy. The PMF-resolved closure (Option A) is a budgeted follow-up - see discovery_implications]
study-30 reactive transport + study-29 kinetics (real libRoadRunner reaction universe) coupled [in-workspace]
Vivarium coupling composite: metabolism <-> membrane via permeability-gated metabolite retention
composition / k_deg boundary sweep to locate the self-maintenance window
measured permeability / CAC / phase-stability benchmarks for independent validation (evidence standard #6)

model_approach.prose: Study 32 is where the membrane stops being a free parameter and starts following from the chemistry. og-31 showed the benefit of a membrane under a reduced-coupling proxy (retention and access as separate knobs); here the amphiphile composition is run through short molecular dynamics to inform a permeability, and that permeability - not a chosen number - sets how well the compartment retains its metabolites. The metabolism then runs inside that boundary. The hard rules are the campaign's evidence standard: input fluxes are held exactly equal to a no-endogenous-membrane ablation (any benefit is a margin over the control, not more feed), and self-maintenance is judged on the measurable criterion - net amphiphile production at least matching degradation AND beating the ablation on flux or persistence - not on a declaration of autopoietic closure. The MD method is Option B (a short structural-observable mapping), chosen as the first cut; the PMF-resolved closure (Option A) is tracked as a budgeted follow-up. The wording stays precisely MD-informed, not PMF-resolved.

decision_test: At input fluxes held equal to a no-endogenous-membrane ablation, the compartmented system must (i) maintain membrane integrity - net amphiphile production >= degradation, the membrane rebuilt by the metabolism against its own decay - AND (ii) exceed the ablation on productive flux or persistence, with the membrane permeability informed by short molecular dynamics of the composition rather than imposed. Failing either is a reported negative (not self-maintaining, or a net cost), not tuned (evidence standard #6, #8). Self-maintenance is taken in its measurable form, not strict autopoietic closure.

findings.statement: At equal feeds vs the no-endogenous-membrane ablation, the compartment SELF-MAINTAINS in the measurable form (verdict qualified). (i) Integrity: net amphiphile production 3.48e-5 >= degradation 1.0e-7 (eta_amph 0.10, k_deg 1e-4/s, M_req 1e-3 M) - maintained. (ii) Benefit: the membrane beats the ablation on persistence (standing organic carbon 1.77e-2 vs 8.96e-3, 1.98x) but NOT on throughput (net carbon flux 0.79x, feed-limited) - so the benefit is retention, not faster chemistry, exactly as og-31 found under the reduced coupling. Self-maintaining = integrity AND benefit = true; qualified because the benefit is persistence-only and the coupling is MD-informed, not PMF-resolved. Guardrail: the metabolism is the sustained A1 carbon-fixing network, not autocatalytic.

Membrane permeability is informed by REAL short Martini 3 CG-MD of the amphiphile composition, not a free parameter: the long di-C16 bilayer (thickness 2.870 nm) is thicker than the short di-C12 one (2.325 nm), and a published solubility-diffusion structure->permeability relation (a labelled proposed_input) maps that to lower permeability (0.256 vs 1.0 rel.) and higher retention (0.661 vs 0.333); retention lowers effective washout and raises the standing pool, so composition informs permeability informs retention. This is an MD-informed structural proxy, NOT a PMF-resolved permeability (Option A, study og-32a). It tightens the composition->permeability->retention chain that og-31 approximated with a reduced-coupling proxy.

Study 32 takes full Gate C on an MD-informed first cut (Option B): composition-informed permeability->retention with the measurable self-maintenance criterion (integrity + persistence benefit over the matched ablation), verdict qualified - advancing og-31's partial, reduced-coupling result by deriving retention from a real MD observable rather than a free knob. The matched-null is the no-endogenous-membrane ablation at equal feeds; self-maintenance is the measurable criterion, not strict autopoietic closure. The result is windowed (integrity holds up to k_deg <= ~0.01/s; the persistence benefit tracks the MD composition). The PMF-resolved permeability (Option A, og-32a) is the gold-standard budgeted follow-up that would re-test the verdict under a structurally-resolved permeability.

limitations: Permeability method = Option B (MD-informed structural proxy), chosen as the first cut: short Martini 3 CG-MD of two chain-length compositions (DLPC di-C12 / DPPC di-C16 phosphatidylcholine bilayers - tractable, well-parameterized Martini stand-ins for the amphiphile chain-length axis / og-17's C2 elongation, NOT the actual endogenous fatty-acid amphiphiles) -> bilayer thickness -> effective permeability via a published solubility-diffusion structure->permeability relation. Only the monotone SHAPE of that relation is claimed; its constants (P0, d0, lambda, P_half) are a labelled proposed_input pending calibration to a measured composition-resolved permeability dataset at vent conditions. This is MD-informed, strictly more real-MD than og-31's retention/access proxy, but NOT a PMF-resolved permeability - Option A (the full PMF+diffusion closure in a real viva-md-membrane wrapper) is many GPU-hours per composition and is tracked as a compute-budgeted follow-up (og-32a) in discovery_implications, not a hidden caveat.

The self-maintenance criterion is the measurable form (net amphiphile production >= degradation AND beating a matched no-endogenous-membrane ablation at equal feeds), deliberately NOT strict autopoietic closure (noted as a possible later tightening). Membrane integrity uses declared model parameters (eta_amph 0.10 = fraction of productive carbon flux routed to amphiphile elongation; k_deg hydrolysis rate; M_req required membrane pool) that were NOT tuned to pass - the margin and the k_deg window are reported, and a higher degradation rate (k_deg > ~0.01/s) would flip integrity to a reported net cost.

The MD bilayers were short NVT runs (72 lipids, ~1 ns, CPU), so bilayer thickness is a short-MD estimate (the composition DIFFERENCE, not the absolute value, is the robust signal); area-per-lipid was held by the fixed box and is not used. The enclosed metabolism is the sustained A1 carbon-fixing network, not autocatalysis (A2 refuted under vent conditions). A net-cost outcome would be an accepted negative, reported not tuned.

resolved_uncertainties: Permeability-method scope (Option A vs B), resolved by Eran (via coordinator): chosen = Option B - short Martini CG-MD of the amphiphile composition yields a composition-responsive structural observable (bilayer thickness) mapped to an effective permeability via a published structure->permeability relation (a proposed_input). MD-informed, strictly more real-MD than og-31's retention/access proxy, but NOT a PMF-resolved permeability. Deferred = Option A (the full PMF + diffusion permeability closure in a real viva-md-membrane wrapper): multi-day, heavy-GPU per composition, compute-budget gated - tracked as the follow-up below, not buried as a limitation. So full Gate C is taken on an MD-informed first cut (B), with PMF-resolved permeability (A) a budgeted follow-up.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether a PMF-resolved permeability (Option A) would change the Gate C self-maintenance verdict versus the MD-informed first cut (Option B) - i.e. whether the published structure->permeability relation is accurate enough at vent composition and ionic strength that the verdict does not move under the gold-standard closure.

followup_study_proposals.title: Full PMF-resolved membrane permeability (gold-standard viva-md-membrane)
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Study 32 takes full Gate C on an MD-informed first cut (Option B: bilayer thickness mapped to permeability via a published relation). Option A - a real viva-md-membrane wrapper computing permeability from a potential-of-mean-force plus diffusion closure for each amphiphile composition - is the gold-standard test of whether the Gate C self-maintenance verdict (currently qualified) holds under a structurally-resolved permeability rather than a structure->permeability proxy.
followup_study_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: Composition -> PMF(z) for metabolite permeation plus position-dependent diffusion -> permeability, replacing the published structure->permeability relation with a first-principles closure.
followup_study_proposals.compute_budget_note: Multi-day, heavy-GPU per composition; compute-budget gated - scheduled when GPU budget allows.
